It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former rank was prefectural shrine. Revered by confectionery makers as the "progenitor deity of sweets"<ref name="mainichi-np-2014-4-20" />, it has branch shrines across Japan. {{nihongo|'''Nakashima Shrine'''|中嶋神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tajima Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
The principal deity is {{ill|Tajimamori|Q11316133|qid=Q11316133|lt=Tajimamori-no-Mikoto}}<ref name="mainichi-np-2014-4-20" />, with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amenoyukawatano-no-Kami}} as associated deity.

Tajimamori-no-Mikoto is said to be a fifth-generation descendant of Amenohiboko and, by order of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}} recorded in the '{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}', brought back from {{ill|Tokoyo no kuni|ja|常世の国|ko|토코요국|simple|Tokoyo|zh|常世國|qid=Q11060259}} the "Tokijiku no Kagu no Mi" (the {{ill|Tachibana orange|fr|Citrus tachibana|ja|タチバナ|lt|Miltuotasis citrinmedis|uk|Тачибана|zh|橘柑|qid=Q11121938|lt=tachibana}} citrus)<ref>Suinin chronicle, postscript section, 3rd month day 12 (corresponding to {{ill|Emperor Keikō|Q329723|qid=Q329723}} year 2).</ref>. Because tachibana (prototype of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=mikan}} and other {{ill|Citreae|ja|柑橘類|qid=Q3216053}}) was regarded as a top-class confection ingredient, he is revered as deity of confectionery and citrus ancestor deity<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Yoroku: "Tokoyo no Kuni" and ancient Japanese...|url=https://mainichi.jp/articles/20171227/ddm/001/070/112000c|website=Mainichi Shimbun|accessdate=2021-11-25|language=ja}}</ref>. He is also regarded as a sericulture deity because he is said to have settled at the present site, reclaimed the land, and encouraged {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=sericulture}}.

Amenoyukawatano-no-Kami was deity of Ami Shrine, merged in the medieval period, and is ancestral deity of the Toritori no Muraji clan. According to the Nihon Shoki, he captured a swan for prince {{ill|Homutsuwake no Mikoto|ja|誉津別命|qid=Q11631423}} by imperial order<ref>Suinin chronicle, year 23 entry.</ref>. One theory says he was enshrined near Wananami no Minato, where the swan was captured in the {{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}<ref>However, the Kojiki does not name Amenoyukawatano-no-Kami; it says the swan was captured by Yamanobe no Ōtaka (Suinin record).</ref>.

== History ==
According to '{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kokushi Monjo}}'<ref>"Kokushi Monjo" is said to have been compiled in {{ill|Ten'en|de|Ten’en|fa|تنئن|fr|Ère Ten'en|ia|Tenen|id|Tenen|ja|天延|ko|덴엔|ru|Тэнъэн|simple|Ten'en|sr|Тенен|tr|Ten'en|uk|Тен'ен|zh|天延|zh_yue|天延|qid=Q1327245}} 3 (975) by a person called Yōkō Mashika, and is treated as doubtful, though some see old traditions in it (Keiichi Imai, 'Amenohiboko,' Sōgeisha, 1966). See also "{{ill|koshi koden|ja|古史古伝|ko|고사고전|qid=Q11410976}}".</ref>, in {{ill|Empress Suiko|Q298057|qid=Q298057}} 15 ({{ill|606|ab|606|af|606|am|606 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|606|ar|606|ary|606|arz|606|ast|606|avk|606|az|606|azb|۶۰۶ (میلادی)|be|606|be_x_old|606|bg|606|bn|৬০৬|bpy|মারি ৬০৬|br|606|bs|606.|ca|606|cdo|606 nièng|ceb|606|ckb|٦٠٦|crh|606|cs|606|cv|606|cy|606|da|606|de|606|el|606|eml|606|eo|606|es|606|et|606|eu|606|fa|۶۰۶ (میلادی)|fi|606|fo|606|fr|606|fy|606|ga|606|gan|606年|gd|606|gl|606|he|606|hi|606|hr|606.|ht|606 (almanak jilyen)|hu|606|hy|606|id|606|io|606|it|606|ja|606年|jv|606|ka|606|kk|606 жыл|ko|606년|la|606|lb|606|lij|606|lmo|606|lt|606 m.|map_bms|606|mdf|606|mg|606|mhr|606|mk|606|mr|इ.स. ६०६|mrj|606 и|ms|606|mzn|۶۰۶|nah|606|nap|606|nds|606|new|सन् ६०६|nl|606|nn|606|no|606|nso|606|oc|606|or|୬୦୬|os|606-æм аз|pl|606|pnb|606|pt|606|qu|606|ro|606|ru|606 год|rue|606|sa|६०६|scn|606|sd|606ع|se|606|sh|606.|shn|606|si|606|sk|606|sl|606|sq|606|sr|606|su|606|sv|606|sw|606|tg|Соли 606|th|พ.ศ. 1149|tk|606|tl|606|tly|606|tr|606|tt|606 ел|uk|606|ur|606ء|uz|606|vec|606|vi|606|vls|606|war|606|wuu|606年|xmf|606|zh|606年|zh_min_nan|606 nî|zh_yue|606年|qid=Q31043}}), Miyake no Kishi, a seventh-generation descendant of Tajimamori, began enshrining Tajimamori as ancestral deity. The name "Nakashima" is explained by saying Tajimamori's tomb appears like an island in the pond of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Emperor Suinin's mausoleum}}. In the medieval period, four shrines in Ami-gō (Ariko Shrine, Amuka Shrine, Ami Shrine, and Kasumi Shrine) were merged and it was called "Gosha Daimyōjin," but later all except Ami Shrine (Amenoyukawatano-no-Kami) were separated.

October it was promoted to prefectural shrine.

== Festival ==
The {{ill|Reisai|Q11385469|qid=Q11385469}} is held on the third Sunday of April, also called the '''Confectionery Festival''' and '''Kikkasai''' (Tachibana Flower Festival). Many confectionery industry representatives from across Japan attend and pray for prosperity.

== Shrine buildings ==
The honden is {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684|lt=niken-sha nagare-zukuri}} with {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}} roofing. After a fire during the {{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078}} period ({{ill|1394|Q6398|qid=Q6398}}-{{ill|1428|Q6315|qid=Q6315}}), it was rebuilt in {{ill|Shōchō|Q1193070|qid=Q1193070}} 1 ({{ill|1428|Q6315|qid=Q6315}}). It is designated {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}} as a structure well showing features of the mid-{{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}}.

== Access ==
*From {{ill|Toyooka Station (Hyōgo)|Q871612|qid=Q871612|lt=Toyooka Station}} on JR {{ill|San'in Main Line|Q1135170|qid=Q1135170}}, take {{ill|Zentan Bus|Q11389110|qid=Q11389110}} to Okuno and get off at "Nakashima Jinja" stop, or take bus to {{ill|Izushi|Q11395756|qid=Q11395756}} via Kami and walk 15 minutes from "Morio-guchi" stop.
